title: Precision binning & batching capacity matrix (regional snapshot)
content:
Purpose:
This sheet captures a compact, actionable snapshot of how precision (quantization) and batching heuristics interact with GPU fleet capacity across regions. The goal is to provide engineering and capacity planners a quick decision surface for: 1) expected token throughput per unit capacity, 2) observable quality deltas for representative workloads, and 3) cost and utilization implications for short-term capacity moves (next 60–90 days).

Assumptions & definitions:
- Workloads: three synthetic representative workload profiles generated from customer traces: chat-short (mean 32 tokens/request), chat-med (mean 120 tokens/request), embed-long (mean 512 tokens/request).
- GPUs: H100-80GB (primary inference), A100-80GB (fallback), L4-48GB (cost-sensitive).
- Precisions: FP16 (baseline), INT8, Q4_M (4-bit mixed), and Q3_B (3-bit experimental binning).
- Batching modes: none (sync), adaptive-continuous (server groups batching across requests with 40ms latency SLO), and large-fixed (max batch used for throughput experiments).
- Quality metric: relative mean log-likelihood proxy (RMLL) and prompt-specific answer-accuracy delta (percentage point change vs FP16 baseline on eval set).
- Cost: normalized token-unit cost per 1M tokens on each GPU type (operational cost + cloud instance).
- Target utilization: values model the effective % of GPU cycles used for inference (after overheads/garbage).

Matrix (summary):
Columns: region | gpu | precision | batching | workload | tokens/sec per GPU | quality delta vs FP16 | normalized cost per 1M tokens | implied throughput per reserved unit (1 reserved H100 equiv) | utilization estimate

Rows (examples):
- us-west | H100 | FP16 | adaptive | chat-short | 5,500 | 0.0% RMLL | $28 | 5,500 tokens/s | 68%
- us-west | H100 | INT8 | adaptive | chat-short | 8,200 | -1.8% RMLL | $20 | 8,200 tokens/s | 78%
- us-west | H100 | Q4_M | adaptive | chat-short | 10,900 | -3.9% RMLL | $17 | 10,900 tokens/s | 83%
- us-west | H100 | Q3_B | adaptive | chat-short | 13,600 | -7.5% RMLL | $14 | 13,600 tokens/s | 87%

- eu-west | A100 | FP16 | adaptive | chat-med | 1,100 | 0.0% RMLL | $36 | 1,100 tokens/s | 62%
- eu-west | A100 | INT8 | adaptive | chat-med | 1,650 | -2.2% RMLL | $26 | 1,650 tokens/s | 70%
- eu-west | A100 | Q4_M | adaptive | chat-med | 2,180 | -4.5% RMLL | $22 | 2,180 tokens/s | 76%

- apac-sg | L4 | FP16 | large-fixed | embed-long | 360 | 0.0% RMLL | $18 | 360 tokens/s | 56%
- apac-sg | L4 | INT8 | large-fixed | embed-long | 520 | -2.9% RMLL | $13 | 520 tokens/s | 66%
- apac-sg | L4 | Q4_M | large-fixed | embed-long | 740 | -6.8% RMLL | $10 | 740 tokens/s | 73%

Notes on the numbers:
- Throughput measured with production-like runtime including KV cache warmup, continuous batching overhead, and network latencies observed in region. Values are median-of-50 runs.
- Quality delta is workload-weighted average vs FP16 on held-out eval sets representative of customer tasks. Negative means degradation.
- Normalized cost accounts for instance hourly price, amortized NVLink/host overhead, and average tokenize/runtime overheads.

Sensitivity slices (quick checks):
1) Latency SLO shift (40ms -> 80ms): adaptive batching increases effective batch size by ~1.5x; throughput lifts ~30–60% depending on distribution but quality deltas unchanged.
2) Workload shift to longer sequences (+50% mean length): KV cache effectiveness increases; INT8 and Q4_M see disproportionate throughput improvements because more time is spent on feed-forward vs attention.
3) Cold-cache bursts: aggressive binning (Q3_B) shows larger variance in quality on first 10 tokens and occasional hallucination spikes — recommended to avoid Q3_B for chat-short.

Operational guidance / recommended levers: 
- Region-level placement: prefer INT8 on H100 in us-west and us-east for chat-heavy customers where 1–3% quality loss is acceptable for 35–60% cost savings.
- Mixed fleet strategy: target 60% H100(INT8/Q4_M) + 25% A100(FP16 reserve for high-quality routes) + 15% L4(cost-sensitive embeddings) for general-purpose capacity in NA/EU during Q2–Q3.
- Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% over 2 weeks with continuous quality monitoring and automated rollback on >2.5 pp accuracy regression.
- Batching config defaults: adaptive-continuous with max latency 80ms for embeddings; 40ms for chat by default unless latency-oblivious workloads.
- Fallback rules: if queued requests per GPU exceed steady-state buffer for 3 min, route 30% of new requests to A100-FP16 pool.

Risk register (short):
- Quality cliffs: Q3_B can produce rare catastrophic quality regressions on rare prompts. Use only behind heavy eval gates.
- Regional procurement mismatch: APAC spot inventory for H100 is variable — plan to keep 2x buffer in A100 or L4 for burst capacity.
- Telemetry blind spots: current RLHF-sensitive prompts not fully covered by eval set; add sample extraction for 1% of production traffic to drift set.

Quick-run scenarios (capacity planning outputs for next 60 days):
1) Conservative growth (+15% token demand): add 10 H100 in us-west (INT8 mix) and 6 L4 in apac to preserve latency SLOs.
2) Aggressive price optimization (-target cost/unit 25%): convert 40% of H100 to Q4_M for non-SLA customers, run 2-week bake with eval set and increase canary to 10% traffic.
3) High-quality tranche: reserve 12 A100-FP16 nodes in eu-west for enterprise customers with strict quality SLAs.

Action items (owners):
- Run 2-week canary for Q4_M on chat-med in us-west (owner: Tomas Becker) — target start 2027-05-10.
- Expand telemetry to capture 1% of prompt payloads into drift-eval set (owner: Marcus Li) — due 2027-05-24.
- Update pricing model with normalized cost numbers here and re-run revenue impact model (owner: Rina Patel) — due 2027-05-14.
